definitions.explanation: A political or social attitude that values tradition and resists rapid change.
The act of maintaining equipment, systems, or facilities in good working order. Common in technical and business contexts.

examples.japanese: {保守|ほしゅ}{的|てき}な{考|かんが}え{方|かた}だ。
examples.english: That's a conservative way of thinking.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{保守|ほしゅ}が{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: Conservatism is strong in this area.

examples.japanese: {保守|ほしゅ}と{革新|かくしん}の{対立|たいりつ}は{政治|せいじ}の{基本|きほん}だ。
examples.english: The opposition between conservatism and progressivism is fundamental to politics.

examples.japanese: システムの{保守|ほしゅ}を{行|おこな}う。
{定期|ていき}{的|てき}な{保守|ほしゅ}が{必要|ひつよう}です。
{機械|きかい}の{保守|ほしゅ}{点検|てんけん}は{安全|あんぜん}のために{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Maintenance inspections of machinery are indispensable for safety.

notes: Two distinct usage domains. In politics, the opposite is {革新|かくしん} (progressive/reform) or {リベラル} (liberal). Common political collocations: {保守|ほしゅ}{党|とう} (conservative party), {保守|ほしゅ}{派|は} (conservative faction), {保守|ほしゅ}{的|てき} (conservative). In the technical/business sense, common collocations include {保守|ほしゅ}{管理|かんり} (maintenance management), {保守|ほしゅ}{契約|けいやく} (maintenance contract), and {保守|ほしゅ}{点検|てんけん} (maintenance inspection). Also used as a する verb: {保守|ほしゅ}する (to maintain).
